clue.text: Study article about trio and take steps to issue a serious warning

indicators.note: moving letters about puts them in a different arrangement

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
to take steps is to act

explanation.surface: A student pores over a piece about a music trio, then takes action to warn someone sternly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the old Riot Act, read aloud to disperse crowds; now it means scolding severely.

clue.text: Triumph of revised caring courses on Saturday

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: A weekend programme of updated care training classes turns out to be a great hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaring success is a resounding hit, a synonym for an outstanding victory or achievement.

clue.text: Suffer in the period encompassing Sion's unrest

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so one piece goes round the other
unrest means disturbance, so these letters are stirred up

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone endures a time of disturbance in Sion, the Swiss town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the period' supplies the outer letters, which are split round the jumbled town name.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer mental anguish, a near synonym of being tormented.

clue.text: One closely following sound story with great complications

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt
complications tangle things, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a story is a tale, which is pronounced the same as tail

explanation.surface: A follower is described as having a plausible tale with plenty of twists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (a sound story), but it signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailgater is a driver who follows the vehicle in front too closely.

clue.text: Inspire Lenin? Even Vyshinskii initially failed!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it
something that failed has broken down, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Could Lenin rouse the people? Even his prosecutor Vyshinsky didn't manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrey Vyshinsky was the Soviet prosecutor of Stalin's show trials.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to animate or stir up, a synonym of inspire in the sense of giving fresh energy.

clue.text: Unholy devil's debts

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil; the 's simply joins it to what follows
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: The devil's IOUs are, unsurprisingly, unholy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, a synonym of irreligious or wicked.

clue.text: African tribesman was the hero of a film, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to the sound of a word rather than its spelling

blocks.clueFragment: was the hero of a film
blocks.note: Tootsie is the 1982 comedy whose hero is played by Dustin Hoffman

explanation.surface: An African man is said to have starred in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is Tootsie (1982), titled after Dustin Hoffman's character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African tribesman.

clue.text: Underground worker returning ill, having been trapped in rocky core

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read backwards
rocky means unsteady, so these letters wobble into a new order
something trapped sits inside something else

explanation.surface: A miner comes back sick after being stuck in the rock at the heart of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, who works below ground.

clue.text: Prior role with new clip that is a part of speech

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: an actor's role is a part
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An actor's former role comes with a new film clip that is part of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' sits inside the material for the rearrangement, not outside it; 'part of speech' is used loosely, as a participle is a verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: A past participle, like 'taken' or 'walked', is a verb form, one of the grammatical forms of speech.

clue.text: Not gregarious at a party

blocks.note: a social is a party or gathering

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps to themselves at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding the company of others, the opposite of sociable or gregarious.

clue.text: All over after Head was found on one knee

definitions.note: descriptive: the bone found on each knee

indicators.note: turned over means the word is flipped end to end

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: After it was all over, the Head was found kneeling, perhaps in prayer or proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the reversed word behind the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, the small bone at the front of each knee joint.

clue.text: Heard one burst into song when it's freezing

definitions.note: describes the process that happens in freezing weather

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken by sound, not spelling

blocks.note: one is I, and bursting into song is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone sang out loud on a freezing cold day.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the forming of ice on surfaces, which happens in sub-zero temperatures.

clue.text: Instrument is first tuned for player

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An instrument gets tuned first, ready for the musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist is a musician who plays the violin, so a player in the sense of a performer.

clue.text: You've arrived when people say things like this to you

definitions.text: You've arrived when people say things like this to you

blocks.note: surface reading: a sign that you have made it, achieved success

blocks.clueFragment: when people say things like this to you
blocks.note: setter's reading: the words of welcome said literally to someone who has just come in

explanation.walkthrough: 'You've arrived' suggests success in life; it actually means simply turning up, when people say hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Greetings are words of welcome, such as hello, offered to someone who has just come.

clue.text: About a circus we left with a following

indicators.note: left here means departed, so those letters go away

blocks.note: we in the object form is us

explanation.surface: Roughly speaking, we left a circus with a crowd of fans behind us.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is the Latin-derived word for approximately, used before dates.

clue.text: Unusual claim: pain created by bell towers

indicators.note: unusual signals letters set out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An odd complaint that bell towers cause pain, perhaps from the ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanili is the Italian plural of campanile, a free-standing bell tower.

clue.text: It's found in great numbers in the shade

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: surface padding: it only dresses the picture of a crowd
letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: Something that crops up in large quantities in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'great' dress the surface; the hidden letters sit in 'numbers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a brown earth pigment, so a shade of colour.

clue.text: Second class artist at the Victoria and Albert's party showing off

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; the ampersand gives no letter

explanation.surface: A mediocre artist preens at a party held at a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold, swaggering display of confidence, a form of showing off.

clue.text: Possibly curb teen madness, originally by lying

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of these letters
originally means at the start, so only the opening letter counts

explanation.surface: Perhaps you could stop teenage craziness by telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' tempts as untruthfulness; here it means reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent means reclining or lying down, as in a recumbent statue on a tomb.

clue.text: Put in place again, having erred or run

indicators.note: run as in colours that run, so these letters bleed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is reinstated after someone made a mistake or fled.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to rearrange, setting things in sequence or position once more.

clue.text: Staff redundancies in the ship's barber shop?

definitions.note: descriptive: what a sailor might get at the barber's

blocks.note: a ship's crew is its staff

explanation.surface: Layoffs among the sailors, or a trim at the on-board barber's.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a crew cut is a reduction in the ship's staff; at the barber's it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, bristly haircut, originally associated with rowing crews.

clue.text: Emperor, without hesitation, takes one article to the shops

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A decisive emperor brings something along to the stores.
explanation.walkthrough: The ER removed is the middle one: EMP(ER)OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store or trading centre.

clue.text: Tea each unit gives companion

blocks.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Tea for every member of a group hands someone a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is a person who accompanies and supervises another, typically a young woman.

clue.text: Furnish in a fit of pique

indicators.note: a fit is a seizure, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone decorates a room in a burst of resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide with necessary items, a synonym of supply or kit out.

clue.text: Glaze made from aseptic ingredients alien discarded

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: the letters of aseptic, taken as the ingredients
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A culinary glaze made of sterile ingredients, with anything foreign thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly used to coat and glaze cold dishes.

clue.text: Said to incorporate university that's monumentally depicted

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body of another

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university is said to have been immortalised in a monument.
explanation.definitionFit: Statued means represented by or adorned with a statue, a monument in stone or bronze.

clue.text: Note greeting bishop getting up to birdsong

blocks.note: Rt Rev, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title, abbreviated RR

explanation.surface: A message of welcome to a bishop who rises early to hear the dawn chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a series of short, high-pitched chirps, as from a bird or insect.

clue.text: Impression of the organisation projected by A1Porterage.com, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged some other way

blocks.note: the 1 stands in for the letter I it resembles

explanation.surface: An imaginary removals website shows off the public face of its business.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporate image is the reputation or public perception a company cultivates.
